_comments: Sample configuration for Snowflake on macOS (verified end-to-end with Snowflake trial account,
same underlying setup as orm_skyway_config_snowflake.json -- this version just uses macOS-style
paths throughout instead of Windows paths, since jx_home/jdbc_driver_jar are literal filesystem
paths and copying the Windows sample as-is leaves you editing C:/... paths on a Mac).
Replace <account>, <database>, <schema>, and <warehouse> with your values.
db_schema: set to the target schema, or leave blank to extract from the URL schema= parameter.
Download the Snowflake JDBC driver from https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/jdbc/jdbc
Snowflake JDBC 3.x users: override jdbc_driver_class to 'net.snowflake.client.jdbc.SnowflakeDriver'
(the 4.x default is 'net.snowflake.client.api.driver.SnowflakeDriver').
jx_home and jdbc_driver_jar below use /Users/yourname/... as a placeholder -- replace
'yourname' with your actual macOS username, or wherever you actually installed the Gilhari SDK
and downloaded the driver. There's no fixed convention -- any path works, this is just an
example that avoids leaving a Windows drive letter in a Mac config.
Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3/M4) note: no docker_platform override is needed here. orm_skyway.py
defaults to linux/amd64 (softwaretree/gilhari is currently amd64-only) and runs correctly via
Rosetta 2 emulation automatically -- this is the default behavior as of orm_skyway.py 1.0.26,
nothing to configure.
Copy to your project root, rename to orm_skyway_config.json, and edit for your database.
Run: python3 orm_skyway.py -f orm_skyway_config.json --phase 1+3
(Phase 3's generated helper scripts are .sh on macOS -- e.g. ./gilhari/run_docker_app.sh --
not the .cmd versions shown in Windows-oriented docs.)
